newsitem.title: USA: Shuttle crew arrives for launch.
newsitem.headline: Shuttle crew arrives for launch.

text.p: Six astronauts arrived at the Kennedy Space Centre on Wednesday to begin final preparations for NASA's fifth visit to Russia's Mir space station.
The five men and one woman were due to go into space aboard space shuttle Atlantis on Sunday at about 4:27 a.m. EST (0927 GMT).
"We are ready to conduct this fifth shuttle-Mir docking mission," shuttle commander Mike Baker told reporters after arriving at the Florida spaceport in a NASA executive jet.
Joining Baker aboard Atlantis will be co-pilot Brent Jett, Jeff Wisoff, John Grunsfeld, Marsha Ivins and Jerry Linenger.
Linenger, a 42-year-old Navy captain and medical doctor, will take the place of U.S. astronaut John Blaha, who has been working aboard Russia's Mir since September.
During his four-month mission, Linenger will become the first American to make a spacewalk from Mir.
"Should be a great mission," he said. "I'm really, really excited to go up there."
Linenger is hoping to end his mission on time in May so he can be present for the birth of his second child, due in late June.
Weather forecasters said on Wednesday they were expecting cold but favourable weather for the shuttle's predawn blastoff.
